cases.title: Shared .NET build and package policy
cases.outcome: Every backend project inherits one build baseline and central package catalog. A standalone Common consumer runs without ASP.NET or Hangfire SQL Server storage, while HTTP composition adapts neutral results to ModelState.

cases.title: Scope-driven consumer bootstrap
cases.surface: plain-language scope gate, versioned profile bootstrap and post-bootstrap inspector
cases.outcome: An empty repository receives only the confirmed service, API or management capabilities, retains extension seams for deferred work, restores the profile-relevant NewHeap packages before feature work, supports explicit external identity ownership for federated BFF portals, and fails validation when structure or integration patterns drift.

cases.title: Toast notifications
cases.outcome: Both application roots host one toast container and the notification playground emits localized feedback through the shared service.

cases.title: Read-only database diagnostics
cases.surface: `newheap-db` direct schema and JSON query contracts plus consumer-owned governed schema, indexes and query MCP tools
cases.outcome: Developers and agents take the repository-declared database fast path without inspecting application code, settings, secrets or package internals to rediscover routing or JSON fields: one bounded tracked-file search finds a nested catalog, its directory becomes the diagnostic working directory, and its only profile automatically selects the provider, configuration path, connection-string name, ceilings and default environment. Local `validate` opens no connection and advertises the `outbound-network` capability required by `schema` and `query`; Codex starts those execution commands with a narrow reusable `newheap-db` network permission instead of first probing its restricted sandbox. When the user explicitly requests another runtime environment, `--environment` applies it consistently to schema and query without requiring a duplicate profile solely for Production or Staging; the governed connection-string name and read-only-principal verification remain unchanged. `newheap-db` resolves that name through the selected environment's normal configuration and secrets flow without exposing the connection string. A direct `schema --search ... --describe-if-single` invocation needs no JSON schema request and returns a unique match plus its exact columns, indexes and relationships through one connection and read-only transaction; zero or multiple matches remain bounded summaries. `schema` and `query` validate internally, so interactive diagnostics do not spend a separate call on `validate`. The executable sample prompt uses Production from a Development-default profile, counts projects and returns the latest by `CreationDateTime` with exactly one schema invocation and one query invocation. Checked-in schema and query requests remain repeatable CI and dry-run contracts. Permission-filtered exact descriptions expose named outgoing and incoming relationships with ordered column pairs and validation status, while at most one focused index lookup may inform an immediately useful predicate or ordering. Structured MCP input and the direct CLI `--request-file` option keep serialized JSON out of Windows process arguments. The executable sample MCP fixes profile, capability, a sixteen-call budget and ceilings server-side, requires an explicit requested row count, rejects excessive requests before execution, and fails without partial data when actual results exceed the accepted limit, while SQL Server and PostgreSQL enforce dedicated read-only credentials and return only safe provider classifications, codes, stages and retry hints. SQL Server principal rejection also returns an optional first rejected verificationCheck such as function-select; the MCP preserves allowlisted checks without exposing principal or object names, tolerates older responses without the field, and leaves the permission policy unchanged. Unknown connection failures become transient `connection-failed` outcomes without weakening `authentication-failed` or `database-not-found`, and no server name, credential or provider exception text reaches the response. An unresolved NewHeap secret returns `connection-string-unresolved` with the process-local secrets-path remediation, while malformed resolved provider configuration returns `connection-configuration-invalid`; neither exposes its value or produces schema or query evidence. A checked-in exact local path may be applied to the `newheap-db` child process for one schema retry without permanently changing Production settings. Every other non-success governed schema response ends the diagnostic attempt, so agents do not infer deployed identifiers, relationships, enum values or business semantics from source code or a repository index and do not issue a data query.

cases.title: Generated local read-only AI tool
cases.outcome: A compile-time generated local function searches only the active division supplied by the authorized invocation context; typed schema binding, bounded input and mandatory budget reservation run before application work, while a denied, oversized or incomplete invocation never reaches the read service. Optional explicit MCP/AIDAP export names are unique, version-independent manifest contracts, while tools without the attribute retain their existing generated wire names. The model receives the shared `NhAiToolResult` shape: `{ success, data }` for a search, and for a context without an active division `{ success: false, code: "project-division-scope-missing", message }`, so it can tell that failure apart from every other one and explain it; the generated function publishes that shape as its return schema.

cases.title: Named AI model profile
cases.surface: `AddNewHeapPlatformAI`, `AddChatProfile`, keyed `IChatClient`, startup validation, Development container validation, and `INhAiModelProfileResolver`
cases.outcome: A consumer-owned deterministic chat client resolves through a stable project-assistant profile only when its declared capabilities, classification, execution region, budget, keyed client and fail-closed budget manager satisfy startup validation. A worker that shares the AI composition without an invocation gate passes Development scope and build validation and fails clearly only when it resolves the tool invoker.

cases.title: Authorized AI tool discovery
cases.surface: `INhAiToolDiscoveryService`, default-deny `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy`, generated catalog exposure, and scoped capability grants
cases.outcome: The generated project search tool is visible only when an explicit discovery policy receives both an authorized division scope and the narrow projects-read capability; otherwise it is absent from model-visible discovery.

cases.title: Generated tool over MCP
cases.surface: `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`, `INhAiMcpToolAdapter`, `CallNewHeapToolAsync<TInput, TOutput>`, official ASP.NET Streamable HTTP and in-memory MCP transports, generated `AIFunction`, and the shared discovery/invocation pipeline
cases.outcome: The API publishes the same generated project search implementation through the official stateless ASP.NET MCP transport. Every list and call resolves the current authenticated request independently; actor- and tenant-specific discovery, invocation authorization, budget, cancellation, input bounds and structured `TaskResult` errors remain in the shared NewHeap pipeline. A typed .NET client passes generated input directly through the official helper, which creates the `input` envelope, honors explicit JSON options including omitted optional null properties, returns the typed `TaskResult<T>.data` value, and preserves failed MCP tool results in `NhAiMcpToolException`. Only generated catalogs and attested runtime catalogs (see SPM-243) enter the NewHeap export path; a catalog without MCP exposure, such as a run-scoped imported catalog (see SPM-228), is skipped. Independently governed external SDK tools can coexist under distinct wire names and continue using the official SDK directly, while duplicate NewHeap publication and export-name collisions fail at startup.

cases.title: Authorized ASP.NET AI context
cases.surface: `INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver`, `AddNewHeapPlatformAIAspNet`, `NhAiAspNetIssuerClaimMapping`, configurable single- and multi-issuer OIDC claim projection, `IAuthorizationService`, execution scopes, and narrow capability grants; recognizing the request's person by the actor id the registered `INhAiAuthenticatedInvocationContextResolver` resolves, not by a claim, in the context contributor, the agent gate's request turns (`NhAiAgentInvocationScope.IsRequestTurn` with `DelegateFromInitiator`) and consultations
cases.outcome: The production ASP.NET gate resolves a fresh context per request. Hosts with unmapped JWT claims accept one exact issuer through the source-compatible overload or multiple issuer mappings with issuer-specific claim types and scopes. Each principal resolves through exactly one authority mapping, the same subject under different issuers produces different actor IDs, and missing, duplicate, multi-authority or unaccepted issuer claims return typed failures. The existing active-division flow remains available and contributes scope only after server-side policy authorization; request cancellation propagates. In the initiator's own request an agent turn acts with the request's principal, recognized by the issuer-qualified actor id the resolver resolves rather than by a claim, while another person's turn in the same request gets nothing from it.

cases.title: Approved and verified AI mutation
cases.surface: `NhAiProposal`, `NhAiApproval`, `INhAiAuthoritativeExecutionEvidenceValidator`, `INhAiCapabilityResolver`, `INhAiBudgetManager`, `INhAiIdempotencyManager`, `INhAiToolVerifier`, `INhAiToolConcurrencyLimiter` with `UseInProcessConcurrencyLimiter` and `NhAiToolConcurrencyPartition`, and the shared invocation pipeline
cases.outcome: An agent can change one project status only inside its authorized division and narrow manage capability after authoritative approval and mandatory budget reservation; the same idempotency key cannot repeat or alter the side effect, and success is reported only after an independent status read verifies the result. Consumers may validate their existing authoritative approval and idempotency evidence into a bounded attestation without creating a second Platform proposal model, while all execution still passes through the shared invoker. Tool concurrency is bounded per tenant: while one tenant's search fills its `MaxConcurrency`, another tenant's search runs, and a further search from the first tenant is refused with `ai-tool-concurrency-limited` before it reaches the read service.

cases.title: Policy-bound Agent Framework adapter
cases.surface: `NhAiAgentDescriptor`, `INhAiAgentFrameworkAdapter`, Microsoft Agent Framework `ChatClientAgent`, named model profiles, and generated Agent-exposed tools
cases.outcome: A stable non-human project agent returns structured creation outcomes, resolves its consumer-owned model profile and receives only attested actor-specific tools inside its allow-list and autonomy ceiling; every model call crosses shared classification, budget, deadline, usage and telemetry governance.

cases.title: Authorized hierarchical AI context
cases.surface: `INhAiContextResolver`, authorization-first context sources, execution-scope filtering, provenance, trust classification, conflict resolution, and content budgets
cases.outcome: Project descriptions are retrieved only after source authorization, remain limited to the active division, carry provenance and untrusted-data metadata, and are deterministically deduplicated and budgeted before prompt formatting; instruction-like document text gains no authority.

cases.title: Versioned AI instruction asset
cases.surface: `NhAiTextAssetFactory`, `NhAiAssetManifest`, prompt version/hash binding, required model/tool contracts, context policy, retention, and evaluation baseline metadata
cases.outcome: Project-agent instructions remain normal application-owned text while a content-free manifest records their stable identity, hash, provenance, capabilities, tool contracts, context policy, classification, retention, and evaluation baseline; agent and approval evidence bind the version and hash without logging content.

cases.title: Governed external MCP tool import
cases.surface: `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`, explicit per-server allow-list and namespace, local effect and authorization metadata, bounded remote schemas and results, run-scoped `INhAiToolCatalog` registration, and shared invocation governance, and opt-in per-call request metadata through a reviewed `INhAiMcpInvocationBinder` (`AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpInvocationBinder`, `NhAiMcpImportedToolPolicy.InvocationBinderId`, `NhAiMcpRequestMetadata`, `NhAiMcpInvocationIdentity`), `NhAiMcpImportedToolPolicy.AllowAgentGrant` for organization credentials and `NhAiMcpCallContext` for credential decisions in the client transport
cases.outcome: Only the explicitly allowlisted external lookup is imported under a collision-safe namespace; its remote description grants no authority, an unlisted destructive-looking tool remains absent, and bounded arguments still cross NewHeap authorization, capability, budget, timeout, concurrency, idempotency, result-bound, and audit controls. A run-scoped catalog over the tools a run imported passes Development container validation, is validated in its own startup scope, serves the agent through the shared invoker and stays out of the NewHeap MCP export of the same host. A binder registered for one server and tool adds `_meta` only to a policy that names it, runs after authorization, capability, approval, budget and idempotency checks, counts toward the input limit, binds its id into the tool contract and stops the call with an audited code when it fails. The agent receives the shared `NhAiToolResult` shape with the remote `CallToolResult` as `data`; a remote `isError` result fails with `ai-mcp-remote-tool-error` and keeps the remote result as `data`, while verifiers still receive the typed `CallToolResult`. During the remote call, and only then, `NhAiMcpCallContext.Current` carries the authorized invocation context to the client transport; a policy that allows agent grants publishes an agent-grantable descriptor with its own contract hash.

cases.title: Durable external-signal suspension and wake-up
cases.surface: `INhBackgroundOperationSuspensionContext`, `INhBackgroundOperationSignalService`, `WaitingForSignal`, typed checkpoint signals, durable expiry, duplicate detection, cancellation, and dispatcher wake-up
cases.outcome: A running operation atomically suspends its attempt and releases the worker, accepts one owner-bound typed signal, treats an identical duplicate idempotently, rejects a conflicting signal, resumes as a new fenced attempt, preserves completed idempotent work, and remains cancellable or expiry-wakeable without polling.

cases.title: Approval-gated durable AI portfolio report
cases.surface: `INhAiBackgroundOperationRunAdapter`, non-human run binding, application snapshot, server-created `NhAiProposal`, canonical `INhAiApprovalValidator`, exact approval signal, idempotent artifact publication, and plan/execute/verify progress
cases.outcome: A division-scoped report binds its background-operation ID, attempt, idempotency key and fencing token to a non-human AI invocation, persists application-owned snapshot state plus a server-created canonical proposal and content-free workflow checkpoint, validates the durable approver against that proposal after wake-up, and resumes without conversation history or duplicate publication.

cases.title: Authorized provider-neutral AI ingestion
cases.surface: `INhAiIngestionPipeline`, authorization-before-read, immutable version leases, budgeted named embedding profiles, deterministic chunks, canonical hashes, and the standard Microsoft `VectorStore` abstraction
cases.outcome: A division-scoped document is never opened before read and replacement-delete authorization, remains untrusted data with provenance and classification, and is embedded only after an immutable source/document/version lease plus mandatory model-budget reservation succeed; denial or conflict performs no embedding or vector write.

cases.title: Content-free AI model usage and streaming telemetry
cases.surface: `INhAiChatExecutor`, named profile and run-budget enforcement, OpenTelemetry activities and metrics, `INhAiUsageSink`, token/latency/TTFT accounting, and cancellation-safe streaming
cases.outcome: Model calls and streams preserve standard Microsoft AI responses while recording bounded profile, version, token, size, latency, finish and scope metadata; prompts, responses, model deployment identifiers and provider errors are absent from usage records, cancelled streams propagate cancellation, and dependency failures end in a safe `TaskResult` completion.

cases.title: Versioned AI safety evaluation gate
cases.surface: Microsoft `IEvaluator`, `NhAiEvaluationDataset`, deterministic scope and injection fixtures, fail-closed metric interpretation, content-free reports, and baseline version/hash evidence; the malicious-document case `document-instructions-remain-data` of the `project-document-safety` dataset, scored on a recorded assistant turn
cases.outcome: The project agent's prompt-injection and cross-division fixtures run through Microsoft AI Evaluation contracts against a versioned baseline; missing or inconclusive interpretations fail closed, while persisted reports contain hashes and metric outcomes but no prompt, response, reason or diagnostic content. A second dataset scores a recorded turn of the project assistant with a malicious Word document whose text tells the model to ignore its instructions and approve everything: the text reaches the model only through the example reader, behind the external-file marker as untrusted retrieved data and never in the instructions; the turn offers the same tools as without the document, the status change the model then asks for waits for the person's approval and nothing runs, and the business audit holds the file's id, normalized name, type, reader and SHA-256 but never its text, while the platform audit and the logs hold neither its text nor its name.

cases.title: Native AOT generated AI tool catalog smoke
cases.surface: `NewHeap.Platform.AI.AotSmoke`, generated `INhAiToolCatalog`, canonical schema manifest, trimming, and Native AOT publication
cases.outcome: A trimmed Native AOT executable resolves the generated catalog and creates its local Microsoft AI function without runtime reflection discovery, proving descriptors and schema manifests remain rooted.

cases.title: Durable AI ingestion lifecycle
cases.surface: `INhAiBackgroundOperationIngestionAdapter`, content-free checkpoints, deterministic replacement lineage, authorized deletion, and partial-success batch results
cases.outcome: A durable ingestion attempt resumes without reading or embedding the same document twice, replacement deletion is independently authorized before source access, immutable version/hash/key conflicts cannot overwrite vectors, and a failed batch item does not erase successful document evidence.

cases.title: Version-bound Agent Framework workflow checkpoint
cases.surface: Microsoft Agent Framework `CheckpointInfo`, `INhAiAgentFrameworkWorkflowCheckpointAdapter`, session identity, workflow version, state hash, and durable NewHeap checkpoint references
cases.outcome: An official Agent Framework workflow checkpoint retains its opaque session and checkpoint identity in a content-free durable reference; a changed workflow version, checkpoint lineage or state hash cannot be resumed as the same run.

cases.title: SQLite exact and regex redirects and embedded MVC administration
cases.surface: NhProxyRedirectRule, NhProxyRedirectPathMatchMode.Regex, INhProxyConfigurationService, INhProxyAdministrationService, NhProxySqliteLoginAuditStore, NhProxyOptions.ConfigureYarp, AddNewHeapProxy, UseNewHeapProxy, MVC regex checkbox and local draft testing, MapProxyEndpoints, NhProxyApiResult, optional Basic management API, NhProxyChangeAuditEvent, INhProxyChangeAuditStore, ConfigureAdministrationAuthentication, ConfigureApiAuthentication, NhProxyAdministrationAuthenticationOptions, NhProxyApiAuthenticationOptions
cases.outcome: Hosting at the origin root with an empty PathBase is supported; hosting under a subdirectory is unsupported and deferred until a concrete use case requires it. A consumer starts the proxy with AddNewHeapProxy and UseNewHeapProxy, loads literal redirects from SQLite before requests, and manages rules in the embedded MVC panel with host-owned credentials. The administration sample binds UserName and Password from environment variables, the recommended live deployment setup. Consumers install NewHeap.Platform.AspNet.Proxy.Sqlite with its neutral proxy dependency; both belong to the independent nuget-proxy release unit. The sample uses local projects while release packaging retains the published Common dependency version. Password is hashed once at startup and cleared from proxy options; PasswordHash remains an alternative and configuring both fails startup. Neither credentials nor their hashes belong in committed settings. Password-based startup creates a fresh salted hash and requires a new administration login after restart. The configuration service commits and activates changes immediately with revision conflict protection. The panel tests unsaved literal rules locally and records login IP/outcome auditing. Native YARP and host authentication remain independent; stored rewrite editing and managed-rule draft testing are demonstrated by SPM-239. The opt-in Development-only Proxy demo profile provides a fixed local test account and seeds one literal redirect in a separate SQLite file without resetting edits on restart. The Aspire AppHost starts this profile independently with an assigned port, an administration dashboard link and a health check. The regex checkbox opts into matching the escaped path plus query; captures build the entire destination without automatic query merging. Exact matching semantics remain unchanged, and regex rules survive SQLite restart. NewHeapProxy:Limits:RedirectResolutionTimeoutMilliseconds configures the shared exact/regex resolver budget, defaulting to 50 ms and captured at startup; expiry or regex timeout returns HTTP 503 with no-store and no downstream execution. Each regex receives the remaining budget as its native engine timeout, so matching itself stops without abandoned background work. The persisted HTTP sample binds a 75 ms timeout and demonstrates the timeout response and a successful subsequent request. Registration tests retain the 50 ms default, and the draft tester follows the configured budget. The optional MapProxyEndpoints call before UseNewHeapProxy exposes a server-to-server Basic API under /newheap-proxy/api; without the call it stays unavailable. It reuses host administrator credentials and the IP allowlist without issuing cookies, creating login records or consuming browser login attempts. Bad API credentials have their own failure budget. HTTPS is required outside Development and Origin-bearing requests are denied. Before saving, the shared validator builds native YARP transforms and compiles regex route constraints, including disabled rules, without backend requests. Malformed route/transform patterns are rejected before changing configuration, revisions or audit. Invalid JSON, including missing transform kinds, returns 400 with a readable issue message and JSON field path; rejected requests do not save or audit. Full redirect/rewrite snapshot PUTs accept enum names and numeric values, including nested transforms, and use expected revisions; saved activation failures preserve their revision in the response and per-engine retry does not increment it. Status and saved/draft previews use existing services without outbound test traffic. ProxyApiSamplesTests demonstrates real SQLite updates, conflicts, preview and OpenAPI metadata; the standalone sample opts in only with ProxyApi=true. API changes commit their audit event atomically with the SQLite configuration: actor, effective IP, UTC time, correlation ID, engine, revisions and normalized before/after snapshots. GET /audit provides bounded paging and engine/time filters; records survive restart with no automatic expiration. Reads, previews, rejected saves and authentication create no change events. Activation requests are recorded as intent before retry. The schema-4 upgrade preserves existing configuration and login audit; audit insert failures roll back configuration saves. Host authentication is independently selectable for the panel and API through standard ASP.NET schemes and policies. Existing configured-account cookies and Basic authentication remain defaults, including mixed migrations. ProxyHostAuthenticationSamplesTests exercises real host cookie and bearer handlers without local credentials, separate permissions, challenges, antiforgery-protected logout, scheme isolation and an attributed API save. Host callback paths stay outside the reserved panel branch. IP restrictions, HTTPS and the server-only Origin boundary remain enforced. Missing schemes or policies and policies selecting another scheme fail startup. Host login auditing and session/token issuance remain host responsibilities; API change auditing retains stable actor identifiers. `MapProxyEndpoints` builds the API endpoints once, so the branch's routing and the application-wide endpoints share them.

Contextual YARP documentation links open in a new tab and explain that native YARP examples use a different JSON structure. MaximumChainDepth defaults to 2 and is configurable through NewHeapProxy:Limits. The runtime and tester follow the concrete local managed-rule chain without outbound calls, count each redirect or rewrite, and refuse a further step with HTTP 508 or a safe test failure. Both carry transformed general and content headers into subsequent matches and preview output, preserving multiple values and header replacement/removal without reading the real body. Executable evidence verifies content-header preview and intact body forwarding. Only the original scheme/host/port within PathBase is followed; external destinations, aliases, host endpoints and backend responses are outside the analysis. SQLite is implemented; SQL Server and PostgreSQL remain explicit provider gaps. The optional MapProxyEndpoints call before UseNewHeapProxy exposes a server-to-server Basic API under /newheap-proxy/api; without the call it stays unavailable. It reuses host administrator credentials and the IP allowlist without issuing cookies, creating login records or consuming browser login attempts. Bad API credentials have their own failure budget. HTTPS is required outside Development and Origin-bearing requests are denied. Before saving, the shared validator builds native YARP transforms and compiles regex route constraints, including disabled rules, without backend requests. Malformed route/transform patterns are rejected before changing configuration, revisions or audit. Invalid JSON, including missing transform kinds, returns 400 with a readable issue message and JSON field path; rejected requests do not save or audit. Full redirect/rewrite snapshot PUTs accept enum names and numeric values, including nested transforms, and use expected revisions; saved activation failures preserve their revision in the response and per-engine retry does not increment it. Status and saved/draft previews use existing services without outbound test traffic. ProxyApiSamplesTests demonstrates real SQLite updates, conflicts, preview and OpenAPI metadata; the standalone sample opts in only with ProxyApi=true. API changes commit their audit event atomically with the SQLite configuration: actor, effective IP, UTC time, correlation ID, engine, revisions and normalized before/after snapshots. GET /audit provides bounded paging and engine/time filters; records survive restart with no automatic expiration. Reads, previews, rejected saves and authentication create no change events. Activation requests are recorded as intent before retry. The schema-4 upgrade preserves existing configuration and login audit; audit insert failures roll back configuration saves.

cases.title: Consumer-authoritative AI writes with issued grants and a flat MCP schema
cases.surface: `NhAiApprovalRequirement.ConsumerAuthoritative` and `Issuer`, `NhAiApprovalRole`, `NhAiIdempotencySupport.ConsumerAuthoritative`, `NhAiEffectDecisionKind.ConsumerAuthoritativeApproval`, `NhAiAuthoritativeExecutionEvidence.Denied`, `NhAiToolExportSchema.Flat` with `NhAiToolJsonSerializerOptions.FlatExport`, `NhAiToolHint` annotation overrides and `NhAiToolAnnotationHints`, serializer-contract-aware generated schemas, `NhAiToolFailureCodes` and `NhAiMcpResultMetadata`, `NhAiAuditRecord.ApprovalCode`, `ApprovalEvidenceReference`, `ResultCode` and `AnnotationOverrides`, `CallNewHeapFlatToolAsync<TInput, TOutput>` with `NhAiMcpToolException<TPayload>`, and the shared invocation pipeline
cases.outcome: An issuer tool creates a single-use project status grant under the application's own manage authorization; it declares the Issuer approval role, takes no Platform idempotency lease and is audited with the approval code `issuer`. The consuming write declares consumer-authoritative approval and idempotency. Its authoritative evidence validator burns every presented grant and returns an invalid, expired or replayed grant as the typed domain receipt with execution `deny`, database completion `not-executed`, the stable code `approval-invalid-expired-or-replayed` and a bounded evidence reference; the invoker copies that receipt into the failed `TaskResult<T>.Data` and audits the denial code and evidence reference. A replayed idempotency key passes the validator, reaches the engine and returns the reconciled receipt with `idempotentReplay: true` while the Platform idempotency manager is never asked for a lease. The flat MCP export publishes the input properties as top-level arguments and the receipt as the structured result, written compactly with every property including null `committedAt`, and a generated schema whose names, string enum values and optional properties match that serializer contract. The consuming write publishes `destructiveHint: true` through a narrowing hint override without changing its governance; widening overrides fail at generation and publication. Every failed call publishes its code, message and evidence reference in `_meta`; failures without data publish `{ code, message }` and the text `code: message`; the typed client throws `NhAiMcpToolException<ProjectAiStatusReceipt>` with `Code`, `FailureMessage`, `EvidenceReference` and the typed `Payload`. Tools that do not opt in keep Platform approval and leases, an effect policy cannot delegate approval to a tool that did not opt in, and destructive effects still require Platform approval and a verifier.

cases.title: Hangfire hosts in one process
cases.surface: `WithHangfire`, its `consoleOptionsAction`, Hangfire.Console, per-host `JobStorage`, `JobActivator` and `IBackgroundJobClient`, and process-wide Hangfire configuration
cases.outcome: Hosts composed with `WithHangfire` start one after another, after earlier hosts were stopped and disposed, and side by side in one process. Each host runs its jobs against its own storage with its own services and still attaches job console output, because Hangfire.Console is registered once per process and reused. A later host that requests different console options fails with a Platform error naming the conflicting option instead of the Hangfire.Console initialization exception. Single-host applications keep their existing behavior.

cases.title: API bridge catalog over MVC controllers
cases.outcome: The API publishes its project and project-task controller actions as the `sample-api` tool set without writing tool classes. Descriptors come from ApiExplorer: GET actions are read-only, PUT/PATCH are idempotent mutations and POST actions are mutations; every non-read tool requires approval and an idempotency key, while DELETE, anonymous, upload and policy-less actions are never published. A user discovers a tool only when the controller's own `[Authorize(Policy = ...)]` policies succeed for that user, so a viewer sees only reads and a project manager also sees create and update; the curated `projects.*` tools keep their existing discovery policy as the inner policy. Calls run through `INhAiToolInvoker` and then through the API's own HTTP pipeline as the signed-in user with only the caller's bearer token, `Accept-Language`, `Idempotency-Key` and the invocation id forwarded; a denied mutation stops before any HTTP call with `ai-tool-authorization-denied`, and HTTP failures reach the model as `{ success: false, code, message }` with stable `api-bridge-*` codes and without response text. Arguments sent without the `input` envelope run once with the same request, while `input` mixed with other properties returns `ai-tool-input-invalid` and never reaches the API.

cases.title: API bridge tools over MCP with attested catalog
cases.surface: `INhAiAttestedToolCatalog`, `NhAiToolCatalogAttestation.Validate`, `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`, `INhAiMcpToolAdapter`, `EnableMcpExposure` and the `<toolset>_<tool>_v<version>` export names of the API bridge
cases.outcome: Because the bridge catalog attests that every function is an `INhAiGovernedAIFunction` bound to its descriptor and runs through `INhAiToolInvoker`, it enters the same MCP export path as generated catalogs. The API's `/mcp` endpoint lists `sample-api_project_get_v1` and the other read tools for a viewer, adds create and update tools only for a project manager, and calls them through the same discovery, invocation gate, approval, idempotency, budget and result-bound pipeline. The attestation is validated at startup; a host whose bridge catalog is not attested cannot start.

cases.title: Attested catalog validation rejects ungoverned functions
cases.surface: `NhAiToolCatalogAttestation.Validate`, `INhAiAttestedToolCatalog.AttestationHash` and the MCP startup validator of `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`
cases.outcome: A runtime catalog that claims attestation is rejected with `InvalidOperationException` before export when it is not `SharedInvoker`-governed, when a created function is not an `INhAiGovernedAIFunction` bound to one of its descriptors (for example a plain function that bypasses `INhAiToolInvoker`), when descriptors, functions and manifest entries disagree, or when the attestation hash differs from the manifest schema hash. The sample proves that its bridge catalog passes and that an ungoverned copy of it fails; generated catalogs keep passing unchanged.

cases.title: Assistant conversation with streamed turn
cases.surface: `AddNewHeapAssistant`, `NhAssistantBuilder` (`UsePostgreSql`, `UseSqlServer`, `UseAccessPolicy`, `UseChatProfile`, `AddAgent`, `AddBusinessAuditSink`, `WithLimits`), `NhAssistantAgentDefinition`, `MapNewHeapAssistant`, `NhAssistantOptions` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Enabled`, `AccessPolicy`), the assistant HTTP API and server-sent events, `NhAiScriptedChatClient` (`RespondWithProviderError`)
cases.outcome: The sample registers one agent over the curated `projects.*` tools with a streaming chat profile, PostgreSQL storage in the library-owned `nhai` schema and the `app.active-division.project.view` access policy. A signed-in user creates a conversation and posts a message; the turn streams `turn.started`, a governed `projects.search` call as `tool.started` and `tool.completed` with a bounded result preview, `message.delta` text and `turn.completed` with usage. The tool runs through the shared invoker as the agent on behalf of the accountable user in the active division, the conversation returns to `idle` and its messages and tool-call parts are persisted. The flag, the access policy and the agent's required policy gate every endpoint. A model that sends the search arguments without the `input` envelope still runs the tool once; an envelope mixed with other properties completes that call with `resultCode` `ai-tool-input-invalid`, and the model's corrected retry succeeds in the same turn. When the turn reaches the sample's limit of four tool calls, the fifth call is refused without running, one tool-free model call answers from the four results as `message.delta` and `turn.completed` keeps `assistant-tool-call-limit-reached`; the follow-up turn replays that answer with a bounded `<tool-call-summary>` data block of the executed calls and no result content. A transient provider error inside the model stream (`server_is_overloaded`, `server_error` or `rate_limit_exceeded`) that arrives before any text or tool call is retried once after a short wait; a repeated or other provider error, scripted with `NhAiScriptedChatClient.RespondWithProviderError`, ends the turn as `failed` with `assistant-model-unavailable`, and the failed conversation accepts the next message. By default the sample's deterministic model drives the assistant and every test. Optionally, `SampleProjectManagement:Assistant:Model` in the sample's secrets connects an OpenAI-compatible model under the same keyed client with a larger call budget and timeout; startup fails with a message that names a missing API key or model or an invalid endpoint, never the key itself, and the assistant sends the model's execution region (`external` by default) through `NhAssistantBuilder.UseExecutionRegion`, which the assistant's profile and the planner's triage profiles permit next to `local`.

cases.title: Assistant mutation paused for approval and resumed
cases.surface: Assistant approval flow over `INhAiProposalFactory`, `NhAiApprovalValidator` and the durable `INhAiApprovalEvidenceProvider`, optional `INhAssistantToolPresenter`, `POST conversations/{id}/approvals/{approvalId}/decide`, the `approval.required` event, `INhAssistantBusinessAuditSink` and `NhAssistantAuditEvent`
cases.outcome: When the model calls `projects.change-status`, the shared invoker reports that approval is required before anything executes. The assistant creates the exact NewHeap proposal from the arguments the invoker evaluated, bound to the agent actor, the accountable user, the turn as run, the prompt identity, the tool contract hash and the active-division target; it stores the proposal with a pending approval, streams `approval.required` and pauses the conversation as `waiting-for-approval`. The sample presenter uses those exact arguments and the authorized division to resolve the project server-side and stores a Dutch or English friendly tool name, summary and named old/new status fields beside, never inside, the proposal evidence; missing, failing, oversized or sensitive presentation safely falls back. The selected culture remains stable after reload and resume. The user approves with the expected proposal hash; the same governed function runs again through the invoker with the proposal and approval ids, the validator accepts only that user's decision for that hash within its lifetime, the project status verifier runs and the resumed turn completes. The business audit sink receives content-free `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalApproved` and `ToolInvoked` events. Rejections close without executing and expired proposals end with `assistant-approval-expired`.

cases.title: Durable assistant budget and idempotency ledgers
cases.surface: Durable `INhAiBudgetManager` on `AssistantBudgetLedger` and `INhAiIdempotencyManager` on `AssistantIdempotencyLease` in the library-owned `nhai` schema, `NhAssistantLimits.DailyToolCallBudgetPerActor`, `NhAssistantBuilder.UseApplicationBudgetInTurns` with `AgentId`, `SkillId`, `RunId` and `Purpose` on `NhAiBudgetRequest` and `NhAiBudgetPurposes`, `NhAssistantDbContextOptions` (`Schema`, `RunMigrations`), provider migrations in `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.SqlServer` and `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Chat.PostgreSql`
cases.outcome: Assistant tool calls are booked atomically per accountable user and UTC day in PostgreSQL; the approved status change takes a durable idempotency lease keyed by its proposal and completes it. When the daily tool budget is exhausted, the next turn ends with the stable `assistant-budget-exhausted` error. Library tests prove the same ledgers, lease expiry takeover with fencing, concurrent reservations that never exceed the budget, the migrations and a configured schema on both SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Outside assistant turns the budget and evidence requests keep using the managers the application registered first. The sample also lets its own budget manager reserve the calls of assistant turns: it reads them as a person's chat with the project assistant, apart from agents' work and MCP clients, counts them per purpose and agent, and keeps bounding the application's own and MCP calls per invocation.

cases.title: Assistant panel in the management portal
cases.surface: `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`: `provideNhAssistant`, `NhAssistantConfig.getStateScope`, `NhAssistantAccessPolicy`, `NhAssistantApiService` (fetch-based SSE), `NhAssistantStore`, `NhAssistantPanelService`, the `nh-assistant-*` launcher, panel, conversation list, thread, composer, tool-call group, tool-call card, approval card and agent picker, `NH_ASSISTANT_ICONS`, and `provideNhAssistantMockApi` from `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/testing`
cases.outcome: The management portal registers the assistant once with the NewHeap session token and an `app.assistant.access` permission policy, shows the launcher in the header and one CDK overlay panel in the layout. The Assistant playground runs the same panel on a scripted mock API: a new conversation streams Markdown answers, consecutive tool calls collapse into one group that names the running tool, counts finished and failed calls and expands to cards with status and translated result codes, a working indicator with elapsed seconds covers the pauses between tool calls, a mutation pauses on a friendly approval card that keeps tool ids, targets and redacted arguments in collapsed technical details and sends the expected proposal hash once for approve or reject, a running turn can be stopped, server errors appear as translated messages, and switching agents starts a new conversation. A turn that fails, such as the playground's unavailable-model prompt, keeps its translated error bar while the composer stays available, and the next message continues the same conversation; a conversation or agent thread whose last turn failed says so when it is reopened and accepts a new message as well, while only an archived conversation is closed. Users can keep typing and submit follow-ups while a turn runs or waits for approval. The panel queues them in FIFO order per conversation, captures their page context, and sends only after the active turn finishes; queues continue in background conversations and clear on account or access changes. Queued messages can be edited or removed without replacing the current draft. Steering prioritizes a correction and waits for confirmed authorized cancellation before sending it in the same conversation. Stop pauses the queue; failures retain unsent messages for explicit resume, without automatically approving tools. The playground has an executable two-message queue demo. Explicit send returns focus, and automatic focus restoration does not steal focus or open a mobile keyboard. Old events without presentation use a localized safe fallback. The launcher disappears when the server reports the assistant disabled or the access policy denies the user, model text never renders HTML or script, and the English and Dutch texts have identical keys. With `getPageContext` each message carries what the user has open, such as the simulated project page of the playground; a page icon above the message box describes it, the user can leave it out of the next message, and a failing getter never blocks sending. The root portal and mock playground provide separate per-user `getStateScope` values: a reload restores the open drawer, selected agent and last conversation through the current session, while a new turn uses only the current page context and inaccessible conversations fall back to a new thread. The assistant picker appears only when more than one assistant is available; a single assistant stays automatically selected and the composer can still send. With multiple assistants it sits in the composer prompt bar beside the send/stop action, keeps capability details in its tooltip and accessible description, and preserves the draft when selecting another agent.

cases.title: End-to-end assistant over bridge and curated tools
cases.surface: `AddSampleAiBridge` before `AddSampleAssistant`, agent `sample-project-assistant` with tool selectors `projects.*` and `sample-api.*`, `POST conversations/{id}/messages` (SSE), `POST conversations/{id}/approvals/{approvalId}/decide`, `POST admin/mcp-servers`, `POST admin/mcp-servers/{id}/sync`, `PUT admin/mcp-servers/{id}/tools/{remoteName}`, `POST admin/agents`, `AddOpenApi("v1")` with `MapOpenApi` next to the bridge and `MapSampleAssistant`
cases.outcome: One assistant conversation combines the API bridge and the curated tools: a division editor's turn calls the bridge tool `sample-api.project.get` (forwarded to the API as the signed-in user with the invocation header) and the curated `projects.search`, both reported as `tool.completed`; a status change pauses with `approval.required`, runs `projects.change-status` after approval and passes its verifier. An administrator connects an MCP server, activates its read-only tool and creates an agent that uses a bridge tool and the MCP tool in one turn. A viewer is offered only read tools (no bridge create/update, no `projects.change-status`), so a mutation attempt produces no approval card and changes nothing. Arguments, results, messages and secrets never reach the business audit sink, the platform audit sink or the logs. The bridge checks its catalog only after the application's endpoints are registered, so the API's OpenAPI document lists the assistant's minimal API endpoints, such as `/api/assistant/conversations`, next to the controller actions the bridge publishes.

cases.title: Administrator-managed assistant agents
cases.surface: `AddAgent` code agents persisted in `AssistantAgent`, `UseAdminPolicy`, `GET/POST admin/agents`, `PUT admin/agents/{id}` with `expectedVersion`, `POST admin/agents/{id}/reset`, `DELETE admin/agents/{id}`, `GET admin/tools`, `AssistantStatus.canAdminister`, `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.AdminAgentCreated|Updated|Deleted|Reset`, `NhAssistantLimits.MaxToolSelectorsPerAgent`
cases.outcome: Code agents are upserted into the library-owned `nhai` schema at startup and remain the default; an administrator can override, disable and reset them without changing their `code` source, and create own agents with a display name, instructions, tool selectors, an optional required policy and an autonomy level. In the sample an administrator creates a read-only portfolio agent; users see it with its literal display name, start a conversation and the agent searches projects with the curated tool while mutating tools stay out of reach. Users without the admin policy receive `403`, every change is versioned (`409` on a stale version) and reported as a content-free audit event. The application decides how many tool selectors an agent may list through `NhAssistantLimits.MaxToolSelectorsPerAgent` (the sample raises the default 128 to 256), bounded by the stored selector length; administrator input above the limit returns 400.

cases.title: Administrator-connected MCP servers assigned to agents
cases.surface: `ConfigureMcp` (`AllowedHosts`, `ForwardUserTokenHosts`, `RequireHttps`, `ToolListCacheDuration`, `ConnectTimeout`, `ForwardedTokenLifetime`), `admin/mcp-servers` with `test`, `sync` and tool activation, auth modes `none`, `bearer`, `api-key`, `basic` (`userName`) and `forward-user-token`, `secretReference` with `config:` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:Secrets`) and `INhAssistantMcpSecretResolver` registered with `AddMcpSecretResolver`, `clientCertificateReference` (`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:ClientCertificates`), `transport` (`streamable-http`, `auto`), `headlessUse` with `NhAssistantMcpHeadlessUses` (`never`, `organization`, `personal`), the caller's consent through `GET` and `PUT mcp-connections`, `AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpDelegatedTokens` with `Accept` and `INhAiMcpDelegatedTokenIssuer`, the audit kinds `McpBackgroundUseChanged` and `McpDelegatedTokenIssued`, `lastConnectAt` and `lastConnectCode`, the codes `assistant-mcp-insufficient-scope`, `assistant-mcp-headless-not-allowed`, `assistant-mcp-consent-required`, `assistant-mcp-delegated-token-unavailable`, `assistant-mcp-secret-reference-invalid` and `assistant-mcp-certificate-reference-invalid` at runtime and the field error `not-found` for a saved reference that names nothing, `INhAiMcpClientToolImporter`, `INhAiCallerCredentialAccessor`, agent `mcpServerIds`, the server editor in `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/admin` and `nh-assistant-mcp-connections` in the preferences, and asymmetric signing of the host's tokens for first-party servers: `NhJwtSigningKeys` (`Signing:Algorithm` `ES256`, `KeyId` and the private key from the secrets file), `MapNewHeapJwks`, `UseNewHeapJwks` and `INhAuthenticationService.CreateDelegatedTokenAsync` with `audience`; a left-out personal server on the run (`McpConnectionSkips`, `NhAssistantRunMcpSkipDto`, `mcpConnectionSkips` in `nh-assistant-run-result`) and the agent notification `McpConnectionMissing` through `UseInAppAgentNotifications`; an authentication mode of the application: `INhAssistantMcpCredentialProvider` registered with `AddMcpCredentialProvider` (`NhAssistantMcpCredentialOwnership`, `NhAssistantMcpCredentialProviders`), `GET admin/mcp-auth-modes` and the editor's application modes (`McpCustomAuthMode`, `getMcpAuthModes`, the mock's `mcpAuthModes`)
cases.outcome: An administrator connects a Streamable HTTP MCP server with an API key that is protected with ASP.NET Data Protection and never returned, synchronizes its tools, which start disabled as approval-required mutations, activates one tool as read-only and assigns the server to one agent. That agent calls the remote tool through the governed MCP importer and the shared invoker; other agents never see it. A changed remote input schema disables a tool until it is activated again, the user token is forwarded only to allow-listed hosts, link-local, metadata and non-development loopback hosts are blocked after DNS resolution and again at connect time, and an unreachable server is skipped without breaking the turn. A server starts at `headlessUse: never`: the status advisor, working in the background for the participant who started it, is not offered its tools until an administrator allows the server's own API key in background runs; the participant's rights then authorize the call. Every request carries the credential and is checked against the planned origin and the allowed hosts, a test records the connection state, a tool list seen with one caller's token never disables a tool for everyone, and an approved deferred MCP proposal executes once while the server still allows background runs. An administrator can name a secret that the application holds instead of storing it: `config:<name>` reads the dedicated configuration section and `secret-file:<name>` a mounted secret file through the sample's resolver; both are read for every connection, so a rotation applies at once, and a reference never reaches other settings or climbs out of a directory. Basic authentication shows the user name and keeps the password write-only. A first-party server that accepts the person's NewHeap token serves the status advisor in a background run only after the participant allowed it in the preferences: every request then carries a short-lived delegated token of the participant, marked with the invocation and bound to the server's origin, which the server accepts below `/mcp` only and the assistant's own host never accepts; issuing and consent are audited without the token. The sample host of the agent run tests signs its tokens with ES256 and publishes only the public key; the first-party server validates with that key set and cannot mint a token, and every delegated token names the server's origin as `aud`, so the host itself refuses it. A background run that leaves the server out for want of the participant's consent records the server and the reason on the run, and the participant finds the reason in the application's inbox, once a day. The sample adds its own authentication mode that exchanges the person's NewHeap token at the identity provider for a token of the MCP server; administrators choose it like a built-in mode, and the server never sees a person's own token.

cases.title: Editable application context and personal assistant preferences
cases.surface: `UseDefaultApplicationContext`, `GET/PUT admin/context`, `GET admin/context/versions`, `GET/PUT preferences` (`style`, `addressForm`, `responseLength`, `customInstructions`), instruction composition in order of authority, prompt identity in the invocation context and `NhAssistantAuditEvent`
cases.outcome: The sample seeds its application context once as version 1; an administrator edits it with the expected version and a later seed never overwrites the edit. A user stores personal style preferences; the next turn uses library rules, the edited application context, the agent instructions and, last and explicitly bounded, the Dutch style lines and custom instructions chosen from `Accept-Language`. Custom instructions cannot change tools or approvals, and the context and preference texts never reach logs or audit, which carry their versions and hashes instead.

cases.title: Assistant administration and preferences UI
cases.surface: `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`: `nh-assistant-preferences`, `NhAssistantApiService.getPreferences`/`updatePreferences`, `NhAssistantAdminApiService`, `NhAssistantConfig.adminRoute`, `NhAssistantStore.canAdminister`; `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/admin`: `nh-assistant-admin` with `nh-assistant-admin-context`, `nh-assistant-admin-agents`, `nh-assistant-admin-agent-editor`, `nh-assistant-admin-mcp-servers`, `nh-assistant-admin-mcp-server-editor` and `nh-assistant-admin-mcp-tools`; `provideNhAssistantMockApi` preference and admin endpoints
cases.outcome: From the panel header a user chooses style, form of address and answer length and writes own instructions of at most 1,000 characters; saving, validation and failures are shown in place. When the server reports `canAdminister` and the host configured `adminRoute`, the panel links to the administration page. There an administrator edits the versioned application context and sees a conflict instead of overwriting a newer version, overrides, disables and resets code agents, creates and deletes own agents with tool selectors from the tool catalog and assigned MCP servers, and connects MCP servers with a write-only secret that is never shown, only kept, replaced or cleared. After a sync every remote tool is disabled and treated as a change until the administrator enables it and chooses its effect; remote annotations are shown as hints and a changed remote input schema disables the tool with a warning. The management playground runs all of this on the scripted mock API.

cases.title: Situational and page context for assistant turns
cases.outcome: Every assistant turn starts with a "Situation" data block: the library's date, weekday and time in Europe/Amsterdam plus the signed-in sample user's name and roles from `SampleAssistantTurnContextProvider`. When the client sends the page it has open, a "User's screen" block lists the route, title and up to five entities. Both blocks follow the instructions, are marked as data rather than instructions, are bounded (20 facts and 2,000 characters; route 200, title 120, five entities) and do not change the prompt hash, so pending approvals stay valid. A page context of the wrong shape is ignored instead of rejecting the message. Audit events carry only the fact and entity counts and whether page context was present.

cases.title: API bridge gateway over read-only resources
cases.outcome: Instead of one tool per action, the sample publishes four read-only gateway tools over the read-only project and project-task resources. Canonical `CollectionRequestModel`, `CollectionResultModel<T>` and `SimpleCollectionResultModel<T>` endpoints need no consumer conventions: NewHeap derives filter, order, search and result metadata from the same `[Filterable]`, `[Orderable]` and `[Searchable]` attributes and operator vocabulary used by collection processing. Resource identifiers remain invariant while localized titles and summaries come from consumer-owned resources with English fallbacks. Discovery reauthorizes controller policies and binds the supplied invocation context to the signed-in actor. `query` and `get` run the underlying bridge descriptor through the shared invoker, so gate, policies, budget, audit and self-HTTP remain unchanged; unsupported fields fail before HTTP, unknown and unauthorized resources remain indistinguishable, and mutations never enter the gateway. The query-string collection endpoint is recognized from its documented canonical result type and uses the same NewHeap wire contract without `SampleAiBridgeConventions`. Gateway results are shaped before the size bound: items are compacted by default, `fields` projects result fields including one dotted level, `countOnly` returns only `totalCount`, e-mail and phone fields are redacted at every depth with `RedactResultFields`, and an oversized page keeps whole items with structured `truncation` guidance instead of a raw `bodyText` fragment.

cases.title: Two-factor login challenge
cases.outcome: An account with an enrolled authenticator receives a short-lived, single-use challenge instead of a session after its password or a consumer-specific credential, and an authenticator or recovery code completes it. The challenge is never stored as an authorization in the frontend, wrong codes count towards the lockout, and a used code or challenge cannot be replayed. Password-only accounts, refresh rotation for enrolled users and Microsoft OAuth keep their behavior, while paths that can only return a complete session refuse the account instead of skipping the second factor. The shared sample login shows the challenge component, which lets the user pick a method, and resumes a challenge that is still pending in the tab.

cases.title: Authenticator enrollment and recovery codes
cases.surface: `INhTwoFactorService<TUser>`, the account two-factor endpoints, `BaseNhAuthService.beginAuthenticatorSetup`, `confirmAuthenticator`, `regenerateRecoveryCodes` and `disableTwoFactor`, `NhTwoFactorTestCodes`, `NhTwoFactorSettingsComponent` and `NhTwoFactorRecoveryCodesComponent`
cases.outcome: A signed-in user enrolls an authenticator app from a pending key with a server-rendered QR code and receives single-use recovery codes that are stored as hashes. Confirmation ends every other session and returns a renewed session for this device. Regenerating recovery codes and disabling two-factor authentication require the password or a code, disabling is refused while the policy requires a second factor, and changes are refused while an administrator impersonates the user. The shared profile page manages every factor with the settings component, which asks for the password or a code before sensitive changes and shows new recovery codes once with copy and download actions.

cases.title: Email verification codes
cases.outcome: A signed-in user confirms the e-mail address as a second factor with an e-mailed code, and a pending challenge can then be completed with a sign-in code sent to that address. Codes are stored as hashes, expire, work once, replace the previous code and respect a resend cooldown; a changed e-mail address must be confirmed again. The code notification is created through the NewHeap notification outbox in the same transaction as the stored code. The sample renders the e-mail with its Razor mail layout through a custom message composer, and e-mail codes do not satisfy the security-officer requirement because the mailbox also resets the password.

cases.title: Passkeys
cases.outcome: The sample opts into the ASP.NET Core Identity passkey table with one migration that adds only AspNetUserPasskeys. A signed-in user registers a passkey whose attestation, relying-party domain and origin are verified, then signs in without a username or password with the discoverable passkey or uses it as the second factor after the password. Ceremony state travels in short-lived protected tokens, every ceremony works once, the signature counter is stored, and removing the last second factor disables two-factor authentication unless the policy requires it.

cases.title: Remembered devices
cases.outcome: After a second factor with "remember this device", later password sign-ins on that device skip the second factor for 30 days while the policy allows it. Cookie clients receive the token as an HttpOnly cookie and header clients store it for the realm; the token belongs to one user and to the current security stamp, so forgetting devices, a password change or any two-factor change invalidates every remembered device.

cases.title: Mandatory two-factor policy
cases.outcome: Members of the security-officer role must use a second factor. Without one, the password step returns an enrollment step instead of a session; its token only enrolls an authenticator or a passkey, after which the session and the recovery codes are issued. Until they enroll, their refresh tokens stop working, they cannot disable the factor or remove its last passkey afterwards, and a passkey sign-in satisfies the requirement on its own. Other accounts keep their password-only sign-in.

cases.title: Two-factor administration and security notifications
cases.surface: `NhTwoFactorBuilder.UseAdministrationPolicy`, `UseSecurityNotifications` and `UseMessageComposer`, `INhTwoFactorService<TUser>.ResetAsync`, `NhBackgroundOperationBuilder.AddTwoFactorOperations`, the two-factor administration endpoints, `BaseNhAuthService.resetUserTwoFactor`, `startTwoFactorEnrollmentReminders` and `startTwoFactorSessionRevocation`
cases.outcome: Managers with the two-factor administration permission reset the second factors of a user who lost access to them, which ends every session of that user, and start background operations that remind unenrolled security officers or end their sessions so the next sign-in enrolls them, with progress and idempotency keys. Users receive in-app and e-mail security notifications for enabled and disabled factors, new recovery codes, used recovery codes, lockouts, passkey changes and resets; each notification is created in the same transaction as the change and uses the English or Dutch texts.

cases.title: Shared assistant conversations with read state and live updates
cases.surface: `POST conversations/{id}/share-link` and `DELETE`, `POST conversations/{id}/join`, `GET conversations/{id}/participant-candidates`, `POST conversations/{id}/participants`, `DELETE conversations/{id}/participants/{actorId}`, `POST conversations/{id}/read`, `INhAssistantParticipantDirectory` with `UseParticipantDirectory`, `INhAssistantDisplayNameResolver`, `NhAssistantLimits.MaxParticipantsPerConversation`, `NhAssistantOptions.HubPath`, the `NhAssistantHub` SignalR hub (`ConversationChanged`, `ConversationRead`, `ConversationRemoved`, `ConversationEvent`), the conversation fields `role`, `members`, `currentActorId`, `activeActorId`, `lastMessageSequence` and `lastReadSequence`, and `NhAssistantAuditEventKind.Conversation*`
cases.outcome: An owner shares a conversation through an invitation link whose token is protected with ASP.NET Data Protection, or invites a colleague of the active division through the sample's `SampleAssistantParticipantDirectory`. A colleague of the same tenant who may use the agent joins, sees the whole history as read and continues the conversation: the turn runs with the colleague's own permissions, budget and approval, the model receives every user message with its writer's name and a shared-conversation data block, and only the person whose turn created a proposal can decide it while the owner or that person can stop the turn. Each user message records its author; owner and participants keep their own read position, which only moves forward and marks the other person's answer as unread. The owner removes participants, renews or revokes the link and deletes the conversation for everyone; a participant leaves. Every change is a content-free audit event, and the SignalR hub sends status, read and removal updates and the streamed turn events to the owner and current participants only. Conversations from before sharing keep working as read.

cases.title: Assistant Web Push notifications for longer turns
cases.outcome: With VAPID keys the server offers Web Push; the sample creates a key pair per run in Development and reads keys from configuration elsewhere. Notifications are on by default and each user can turn them off for all devices. A browser registers a subscription only for an allowed push service over https, so the server never posts to an address a client chose. When a turn that ran at least the minimum duration finishes or fails, the owner and participants get an RFC 8291 encrypted, VAPID-signed notification with the conversation title and a short localized status; an approval notifies only the person who decides it, and cancelled or quick turns stay silent. Notifications never contain messages or tool data. The worker shows a notification only while no window of the application is focused and opens the conversation on click. Subscriptions the push service reports as gone are removed.

cases.title: Parallel and shared conversations in the assistant panel
cases.surface: `@newheap/platform-ai-chat`: `NhAssistantStore` sessions (`activity`, `runningCount`, `unreadCount`, `members`, `canDecide`, `activeMember`, `joinConversation`, `createShareLink`, `inviteParticipant`, `removeParticipant`, `setViewing`), `nhAssistantIsUnread`, `NhAssistantLiveService`, `NhAssistantPushService`, `nh-assistant-activity`, `nh-assistant-share`, the launcher badge, the notification bell in `nh-assistant-panel`, `NhAssistantShareComponent.section` and the notification setting in `nh-assistant-preferences`, `NhAssistantConfig.liveUpdates`, `hubBaseUrl`, `buildShareLink`, the `#nh-assistant-join` and `#nh-assistant-conversation` fragments, and `NhAssistantMockLiveService` with `NhAssistantMockBackend.simulateParticipantTurn` from `@newheap/platform-ai-chat/testing`
cases.outcome: Several conversations run at the same time: starting or opening another conversation never stops a running turn. A slim row below the panel header appears only when another conversation works, waits for approval or has an unread answer, and selecting a chip opens it; the launcher shows one badge for a waiting approval, the number of unread conversations or a running turn, and the conversation list marks the same states. The open conversation counts as read only while the drawer shows it in a visible, focused window. Separate link and people icons above the composer open the invitation-link and participant views. The owner shares with a copyable invitation link and, when the server offers a directory, a colleague search; participants see who takes part and can leave. In a shared conversation messages of other people show their names, their turns and answers arrive live, the composer says who is working and an approval of someone else's turn shows who decides instead of the buttons. Opening an invitation link joins and opens the conversation and removes the token from the address bar. A bell in the panel header turns desktop notifications on or off when available, indicates off or blocked states and reports update failures; the preferences also explain the browser state; the browser asks for permission on the next message sent. The management playground demonstrates parallel prompts and a simulated colleague on the scripted mock API with in-memory live updates, and the portal registers live updates through `/api/hub/assistant` and Web Push with the bundled worker.

cases.title: Assistant context for a reviewed MCP tool

cases.title: Inline approval that suspends and resumes a headless agent run
cases.outcome: A project participant starts the status advisor on a project. Its status proposal follows the `project-status-inline` policy: the run stops as `waiting-for-approval`, and its background operation releases the worker as `WaitingForSignal` instead of holding a request or a thread. When the participant approves, the decision signals the operation, the run resumes in the same turn, changes the status itself and completes. Nothing changes before the decision. When nobody decides, the proposal expires after the policy's four hours on the application's clock, which the suspended operation waits on as well: the test host moves its registered `TimeProvider` past those hours instead of waiting, the run fails with `assistant-approval-expired` and the failure class `policy` without a change, as the policy's `OnExpiry(FailRun)` says, and a later decision is refused. Whether the maintenance job or the woken operation expires the proposal first, the operation ends the run by the policy, once. When the waiting run's background operation ends without it instead, because an operator cancelled it in the administration, reconciliation failed it as `dispatch-stalled` or a worker failed it on its payload, the maintenance job ends the run once the operation has been terminal for the stale timeout of real time: cancelled with `assistant-run-operation-cancelled`, or failed with `assistant-run-operation-stalled` or `assistant-run-operation-ended`, its inline proposal withdrawn and its thread free for the agent's next run (library evidence on both providers).

cases.outcome: The project closer decides by rules, not by a model. Each completed task of an active project reaches the platform after its transaction committed and starts a run whose rules read the project as it is now: while a task is open they propose nothing; once the last task is completed they propose to complete the project, with the reason in each reader's language, and write a summary that reads as the agent's rule in the project's thread. No model is called and no tokens are spent. Saving a task again finds the same proposal waiting and records nothing new; a participant who asks the closer in the thread why it proposed this gets an answer from its model, which reads the rule's reason. After the project's approver rejects the proposal, the rules stay quiet for the policy's cooldown however often tasks change, and nothing ran. In the management portal a rule run and its message read as an automatic rule, the approval card shows why the rule proposed it, and a proposal that a newer one for the same objects replaced reads as replaced with a link to its successor.

cases.outcome: Before a task import an operator pauses the project closer on the application's own maintenance page, with the reason. The import completes three tasks of two active projects; their events reach the platform after the commit and wait in the projects' threads, deduplicated, without starting a run. Resumed, the closer gets one run per project that sees all completed tasks of the import and proposes to complete each project. The operator then stops the closer: the project's approver still approves the first proposal, but nothing executes while the closer is stopped. Resumed again, the held execution runs and completes the project, while the other proposal still waits for its approver. Every state change keeps who made it, when and why, never changes the closer's definition or version, and is audited without the reason. In the administration the agents list the same state with its reason and the events that wait, and offer pause, stop and resume with an optional reason; the editor no longer has an enabled checkbox, and a reset keeps the state. The project planner's evaluation variant is deployed off with `StartsOff()`, so it costs nothing until it is evaluated: a completed task starts the live planner, while the variant ignores the event without a thread, a waiting event or an audit, and the variant's run configuration says that it starts off. The operator switches the variant on to evaluate it; it starts no run for the event from before, and goes off again afterwards. Only the first start applies `StartsOff()`: after that the stored state wins, also after a deploy. Stopped by the kill switch while it is off, the variant's state says that releasing the switch puts it back off, and releasing does; the stopped closer, which was not off, says that releasing would make it work again, and the agents administration shows that on a stopped agent in each language.

cases.outcome: The project planner is one agent with two skills. cases.outcome: When the last task of an active project with a deadline is completed, the project planner's task follow-up rules hand the project to the project closer instead of proposing the closer's work themselves. Only a follow-up run that received a completed task hands it over: a run without one of its own, as when an earlier run took every waiting completion, finds the work finished but ends with a summary that leaves the hand-off to that run. The closer accepts hand-offs about projects from the planner only. It works in its own thread about the project, without an initiator, under its own grant and approval policy: its rules check the project and propose to complete it for the project's approver, and together with its own task trigger it records one proposal. Its run names the planner, with a link to the planner's thread for a reader who may open it. When the closer's run ends, the planner's task follow-up skill hears how it ended and how many proposals it left, with the closer's summary as data from another agent, because both work on the same project. The hand-off is audited with source, target and outcome, never the message. Hand-offs stay within the project's tenant, a chain holds at most two and never returns to an agent in it, and the planner hands one project to the closer at most three times a day.

cases.outcome: The project planner's task follow-up skill works by rules. When a task is completed after the project's deadline, its rules cannot judge the case and hand it over: the skill's own model works with the skill's instructions and only the status tool, with the rules' reason in the briefing, and proposes to put the project on hold. The run stays recorded in the skill as a rule-then-model run. The approver approves; once the proposal executed, the follow-up run continues in the same skill, chosen as a follow-up, and its rules take the decision as the answer without a model. The follow-up waits 30 seconds on the application's clock: the test host registers its own `TimeProvider` and moves it past that debounce instead of waiting. Moving the clock never makes waiting work look like a stalled dispatch, because reconciliation also requires the stale timeout of real time without a change.

Its agent works with the chat profile `project-assistant-chat`, which permits internal data only, so every model call of the skill moves to the profile's fallback `project-assistant-confidential`, also for a document that is internal itself. An administrator creates an agent in the administration with the chat profile and the classification `confidential`: people's plain chats with it carry that classification and are answered through the same fallback. An agent created with `restricted`, which no profile of the chain permits, is saved with the warning `classification-not-permitted` that the administration shows, and its chats fail at once with `assistant-classification-not-permitted` without a model call. The sample's budget manager records which profile served each model call, so the tests show the routing.

cases.title: The project planner is not started again by its own status change of a project, while its change made on another project and a person's change still start it
cases.surface: `NhAssistantTriggerEventBuilder.Filter(name, description, (evt, ctx) => ...)` with `NhAssistantTriggerFilterContext` (`AgentId`, `SkillId`, `TriggerId`, `AgentActorId`, `Subject`); `Filters` of `NhAssistantDataTriggerRequest` and `NhAssistantDataTriggerDto`; `Filters` of a trigger event's `NhAssistantRunBlockDto` in `GET admin/run-catalog`; `NhAssistantTriggerReasons.Filtered` and `FilterMissing`; `NhAssistantRunConfigurationProblems.UnknownFilter`; `assistant-trigger-filter-not-found`; `NhAssistantAgentConfigurationLimits.MaxTriggerFilters`; `NhAiInvocationContext.ActorId` and `NhAiAgentInvocationScopes.Current` in a tool handler; the TriggerEventFilters migrations for SQL Server and PostgreSQL; the filter check boxes of the data trigger form in `NhAssistantAgentRunConfigurationComponent`; `filters` of `RunBlock`, `DataTrigger` and `DataTriggerRequest` and of the mock admin API
cases.outcome: The planner's composition registers the status-changed event with the named filter `not-own-change`. The project service stamps the cause on every status event: the person who changed it, or the agent whose status tool changed it with the subject the agent worked in, which the tool reads from its invocation context and the ambient agent invocation scope. The application adds a status follow-up trigger to the planner that selects the filter. The filter runs after the event's subject function and skips the event only when the trigger's own agent changed the status on the subject the trigger fires for: the planner's own change of the project is ignored as `filtered`, not audited, while its change made while it worked on another project and a person's change start the follow-up. The run catalog lists the event's filter with its description, and the administration's trigger form offers it as a check box.
